title: When the Ember Burns Again
premise: Vesper Crane has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot cross its borders, hiding from the court beneath the mountain that bought her soul before she was born. When she finds her name and tonight's date in a century-old prophecy, she flees with three unlikely companions: a disgraced knight, a talking ember-spirit, and the prince sent to retrieve her. As they descend toward the Undercourt, Vesper learns her mentor sold her soul to save the valley itself, and that reclaiming it will unmake the barrier protecting everyone she loves. In the end, Vesper refuses both surrender and theft: she offers the Undercourt's dying king a new bargain—her magic freely given in exchange for her soul and the valley's freedom—and walks out of the mountain changed, bound to no one but the family she chose.
about_author: Petra Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about stubborn girls, bad bargains, and the families we build from strangers.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On her nineteenth birthday, Vesper tends her mentor Maren's herb shop in the Hollow, chafing at its magicless borders. She discovers her exact name and date inked in Maren's locked prophecy book, dated a century past. The beat is quiet dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What Maren Sold
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Confronting Maren, Vesper learns the truth: her soul was sold to the Undercourt before her birth, the price of the valley's protective ward. Maren begs her to run; instead Vesper packs a bag. The emotional beat is betrayal braided with fierce resolve.

chapters.title: A Knight With No Oath
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, brief interlude from Ser Aldric's. At the border stone, Vesper is caught by Aldric, a knight exiled for refusing an order, now hired by the Undercourt as her escort. He lets her go—then follows anyway. The beat is wary alliance forming between two people who owe nothing to anyone.

chapters.title: The Ember That Followed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Beyond the valley, magic floods back into Vesper for the first time, wild and painful. A small ember-spirit named Cindral attaches itself to her, claiming it was born from her sold soul's spark. The beat is wonder shadowed by grief for the self she never knew.

chapters.title: The Prince in the Inn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Prince Kaelen of the Undercourt finds them, charming and exhausted, under orders to bring Vesper home before the king dies and the bargain collapses. Over one long night of cards and confessions, he defects—or seems to. The beat is love kindling against duty on both sides.

chapters.title: Road of Ash
chapters.summary: Group POV rotation. The four travel through a blighted march where previous soul-bargains have rotted the land, seeing what the Undercourt's hunger costs. Aldric's old commander hunts them; Kaelen lies to protect Vesper and is caught at it. Trust fractures; Cindral dims. The beat is the cost of secrets.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath
chapters.summary: Kaelen's POV. They reach the mountain gate, where Kaelen must formally present Vesper or be branded traitor. He chooses treason openly, kneeling to her instead of the crown. Aldric holds the pass alone against the hunt. The beat is sacrifice as proof of love—not romance, but chosen family.

chapters.title: Court of Cold Fire
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the Undercourt, the dying king reveals the final truth: the valley's ward runs on Vesper's stolen soul, and taking it back kills everyone in the Hollow. Maren arrives, having followed, to offer her own soul in trade. The beat is despair at a choice with no clean answer.

chapters.title: When the Ember Burns Again
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, climax. Refusing every offered bargain, Vesper does what no one bargained for: she gives the king her magic freely, not her soul, reigniting his cold fire enough to release all held souls—including hers—before it gutters out. Cindral blazes into her chest. The ward holds on memory, not theft. The beat is defiant grace.

chapters.title: Home Is a Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, resolution. Magicless again but whole, Vesper returns to the Hollow with Kaelen, Aldric, and Cindral-as-cat, none of whom belong there and stay anyway. She reopens Maren's shop, the prophecy book's last page now blank. The beat is quiet joy: family found, duty rewritten, love that stayed.
